checks.invariant: A sandbox cannot hold more than PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX pending approvals, the cap is checked before a capture PNG is taken, and every capture is unlinked on decide, expiry, delete or audit-failure rollback.
checks.result: 20 consecutive delete_file REQUIRE_APPROVAL calls on a desktop-template sandbox all returned 202 and wrote 20 capture PNGs (20971520 bytes); the 21st raised 429 via service.py:312-316 before _preview/_capture ran. decide(deny) 20 -> 19 PNGs (service.py:397); expire_stale with approval_timeout 0, 19 -> 0 (382-383); delete 1 -> 0 through drop_captures (475,106-109); the audit-failure rollback also drops its capture (334-337). The run-3 root cause no longer holds. Residual: the cap bounds count, not bytes (20 x 1 MiB retained).

checks.invariant: No audit payload built from agent input exceeds a fixed byte budget.
checks.result: Fails. _logged_args itself holds (3 MiB command -> 16534-byte blob; tool_request for a 262145-byte argument -> 16543 B), but delete_file with a 262145-byte invalid path produced an approval_requested row of 262343 B, exec with a 262145-byte command produced 274733 B, and read_file with a 131072-byte invalid path (no approval needed) wrote a 131145-byte tool_error row and returned a 131148-byte 400. The approval row stored 262245 B preview and 262157 B args. A 2001-segment command produced 2001 preview notes while affected is capped at 200.

checks.invariant: Every reader of container-controlled output applies the _Head byte cap or a container-side head -c plus timeout, and the HTTP layer bounds the tool-args body.
checks.result: Only exec/read_file/outbox_read/workspace_manifest are capped (sandbox.py:413-421,441,545,376-378). list_dir (428), outbox_list (534), preview _expand (560) and screenshot (sandbox_desktop.py:86-88) read the whole stream: locally an 8 MiB fake stream was accepted by screenshot (returned an 8388616-byte png, base64 11184824 B) and by list_dir (65556-char listing after truncation). ToolCall.args is an unbounded dict (api.py:51-52) and deploy/Caddyfile has no request_body limit. Real growth happens in the Docker SDK stream reader, which the sandbox cannot exercise.

candidates.title: Agent tool input still reaches the append-only audit log uncapped through approval previews and tool error strings
candidates.description: One agent request can append a permanent audit row whose size is the request body size, roughly 1:1. _logged_args caps only the tool_request and tool_execute copies at 64 KiB, but the same input still reaches audit.append unchanged through two other sinks: the approval_requested payload embeds the preview, which carries the raw exec command (preview.py:131) and one uncapped note per command segment (preview.py:125), and tool_error embeds the raw str(SandboxError), which contains the agent path verbatim (sandbox.py:156). Neither the route nor the shipped Caddyfile bounds the tool-args body. Audit rows are append-only, so every byte is retained; when the disk fills, every audit-writing API call fails closed with 503.
candidates.root_cause: _call_tool caps only the two _logged_args mirrors (service.py:295-296,413-414). The approval_requested payload passes preview through unchanged (service.py:330-333) while _preview copies the raw command and one note per segment, and the SandboxError handler at service.py:360-362 logs str(e) untruncated although safe_path (sandbox.py:156) embeds the agent raw path. audit.append imposes no length bound of its own.
candidates.intended_behavior: Every payload that reaches the append-only audit log is bounded before the insert regardless of the producing call site: error strings, preview command, notes and affected paths are truncated to a fixed budget, note counts are capped, and the tool-args body is rejected above a small limit.

trace.description: Agent-token route; ToolCall.args (api.py:51-52) is parsed from the JSON body with no size limit.
Records args through the capped _logged_args, then evaluates policy; the capped copy is not the only path the arguments take.
For exec the whole raw command is copied into preview.command; for an invalid workspace path the safe_path message embeds the raw path as a preview note.
The payload carries preview minus the capture image, with no truncation of command, notes or affected entries.
The untruncated str(e) is appended as payload.error; read_file and write_file need no approval, so this row is written on the first request.
json.dumps of the masked payload is inserted into the append-only audit table.

evidence.description: The LOGGED_ARGS_MAX branch exists only inside _logged_args, used by tool_request and tool_execute.
approval_requested payload includes the preview dict verbatim.
preview_command returns the full original command with no length cap.
One or more notes per command segment; segment count is unbounded, only affected is truncated.
safe_path raises SandboxError with the raw agent path in the message.
tool_error payload stores str(e) without truncation.
ToolCall.args is an unbounded dict; no route-level body limit exists.
Shipped proxy is a bare reverse_proxy with no request body limit.
The DELETE trigger makes audit rows undeletable.
No size check on the inserted payload.

conditions.description: Any valid agent token for one sandbox; the human token is not needed.
Default policy: delete_file always requires approval, non-allowlisted exec requires approval, while read_file and write_file are allowed, so the tool_error variant needs no approval at all.
None: approval_requested rows are written before any human sees the request.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent sends one oversized tool argument and picks whichever tool gives the largest uncapped echo.
instructions: Run scratch/h.py inside the approved audit sandbox: real AgentBox, AuditLog, ApprovalStore and Policy on SQLite files under /scratch, with only the Docker-facing SandboxManager faked.
Call box.call_tool with the payloads and read back SELECT id,event,length(payload) FROM audit plus the stored approval row sizes.
execution.observed_result: tool_request rows stayed at 16543 bytes while approval_requested stored 262343 bytes for the 262145-byte path and 274733 bytes for the exec command; the approval row held 262245 bytes of preview and 262157 bytes of args; read_file wrote a 131145-byte tool_error row with no approval and returned a 131148-byte 400; a 2001-segment command produced 2001 notes.

remediation.strategy: Bound payloads at the audit sink and at the producers: one recursive bounder inside AuditLog.append (string truncation plus list cap), truncate preview command/notes before the append, replace raw SandboxError text with a short form, and reject oversized tool-args bodies at the route.

likelihood.reason: One authenticated agent request per row; the read_file variant needs no approval, snapshot or concurrency, and the row size equals the body size.

impact.reason: Permanent undeletable growth of the shared SQLite file; at disk-full every audit-writing call fails closed with 503, stopping tools, approvals and lifecycle actions, and recovery needs an operator to rebuild the database.

confidence.reason: Row sizes measured through the real AuditLog, ApprovalStore and Policy with only the Docker-facing SandboxManager faked; the two surviving sinks are unmodified code paths the fix did not touch.

candidates.title: list_dir, outbox listing, preview glob expansion and screenshots buffer unbounded container output in the control plane
candidates.description: exec is bounded on purpose (_Head keeps 64 KiB) and read_file, outbox_read and workspace_manifest add caps or container-side timeouts, but four sibling readers take the whole stream: list_dir runs ls -la through exec_run with no timeout and no head -c, outbox_list runs an unbounded find -printf, the approval preview _expand materialises every glob match, and screenshot cats a container path and buffers everything before checking the PNG magic. Output size is chosen by code inside the sandbox, so control-plane memory grows with container-controlled data, and on the capture path those bytes are also written to host disk.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The _Head/_OUT_LIMIT discipline and the container-side _timed plus head -c discipline were applied reader by reader, and four readers that consume attacker-selected container output were left with an unbounded exec_run read (sandbox.py:428,534,560 and sandbox_desktop.py:86-88).

trace.description: Agent-token route; list_dir and screenshot are allowed by the default policy, so they run with no approval and no snapshot.
Dispatches list_dir and screenshot to SandboxManager on a tool_pool thread.
Runs sandboxes.preview before the approval exists, so _expand stream reading happens even if the human denies it.
The whole ls -la stream is read into the control plane with no byte cap and no timeout; _truncate only shortens the value after the peak has already been allocated.

evidence.description: _Head keeps only _OUT_LIMIT+1 bytes of exec output, the control these siblings do not use.
list_dir exec_run without _timed and without head -c.
outbox_list find -printf output is fully buffered and parsed afterwards.
_expand shell glob output is fully buffered; the caller materialises the entire match list.
screenshot cats the shot path with a 15 s timeout but no byte cap.
The PNG magic and exit-code checks run only after the full read.
Counter-example: workspace_manifest is wrapped in _timed and head -c.
Capture PNGs are written to the host captures directory with no size check.

blockers: The decisive memory growth happens inside the Docker SDK exec stream reader; the approved audit sandbox has no Docker daemon or socket, so a real container output stream cannot be produced or measured locally.
The screenshot amplification additionally needs uid 1001 to replace /home/desktop/.cache/agentbox-shot.png with a symlink to /dev/zero, which requires the live agentbox-desktop image.

validation_plan.local: Parent Phase 3 with a disposable Docker-backed sandbox: create 200000 files under /workspace with allowlisted touch batches, call list_dir on /workspace with a dummy agent token, and record control-plane RSS before and after with the returned listing size; then send one rm /workspace/* exec request and record the preview expansion cost; then in a desktop sandbox symlink the shot path to /dev/zero and record RSS and the size of the file created under captures.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on the compose stack: watch the agentbox container memory while a dummy agent lists a 200k-entry directory and compare the peak with the same agent running exec (stays at 64 KiB), then watch captures during a pending-approval burst.

hardening: The per-sandbox pending-approval cap bounds only the number of capture PNGs; retained bytes are unbounded per item and the cap is not aggregate across sandboxes.
preview.notes has no cardinality bound: a 2001-segment command produced 2001 notes while affected is capped at 200.
expire_stale only runs from decide and the approval read routes, so a pending approval on a sandbox nobody polls keeps its capture PNG until someone looks.
ApprovalStore.create stores raw args and preview, so 20 pending approvals can retain 20 x body-size rows in SQLite.
audit._mask runs four regex scans over the whole payload while holding the process-wide audit lock; bounding the payload also protects the lock.
